newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Euro refining margins healthier as gas oil rallies.
newsitem.headline: Euro refining margins healthier as gas oil rallies.

text.p: European refinery margins have started November in a healthy state as gas oil picks up from its recent slide and despite gasoline's fading strength, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

"October was better than September and the gas oil crack was at its highest for six or seven years. And in November, the (overall) margin has been even higher (than in October)," said an economist with one European major.
"We were certainly expecting (the margin) to be weaker, but then gasoline improved greatly and gas oil only came off a little," said another
Gas oil futures are on the march again after a $20 slide which ended on Tuesday.
By mid-afternoon Thursday, November IPE futures were up by over $5 a tonne and the November-December spread had widened by $3 to $9.25.

An opening arbitrage to Asian markets and a rumoured squeeze on the November contract were cited as reasons for Thursday's rally, but analysts say there are reasons to believe the gas oil crack can widen further even without a sudden cold snap.

"Considering the low stocks, the gas oil cracks are on the low side for us, although they are on the upper side of the normal band. We would expect (the crack) to be strong for the balance of the year," said an economist at a Dutch refinery.
Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore said the gas oil crack was unlikely to match October's high. But a more stable level of $40 a tonne would still be high.
"We were expecting gas oil to come off, but (the crack) is still at a historical high," she said.
German consumers' restocking is likely to continue despite large purchases in early autumn.
"German end-users have restocked to some extent. There was a large primary stock drawdown in September and October, but (restocking) is likely to continue," Poynter said.
Gasoline, meanwhile looks ripe to drop even more.
Benchmark premium unleaded barges have fallen $17 a tonne from their October 22 peak of $239.
Traders said the strength has been largely the result of buying ahead of the UK budget on November 26. The government has said it will annually increase excise on auto fuels.
"Gasoline's strength is artificial and all budget related. We'd expect gasoline to collapse fairly soon," Poynter said.
However, some warned that the stress on replenishing gas oil stocks at the expense of gasoline production could prove short-sighted
"The stocks could be rather low in February and gasoline prices could start to rise sharply from then," one economist said.
